hero.title: Pro-level models, in your own profile
hero.lead: Every day, the dashboard models your running with the algorithms we use with elite athletes: the Enduraw Report after each run, your Runner Matrix, pacing plans, lab results. One ecosystem, open to every runner.
hero.alt: Enduraw pacing plan on a laptop, fictitious data: course map and elevation profile coloured by gradient
hero.altMobile: Today view of the Enduraw dashboard on a phone, with sample data

report.title: The Enduraw Report
report.lead: Connect Strava: the Enduraw Report recalculates the pace of every new run for the conditions of the day, so you can compare your sessions with each other.
report.heatDesc: About 0.27% of pace per degree above 15.6 °C, to show what the session is worth in cool weather.
report.windDesc: Headwind and tailwind, taken along your route, to isolate their effect on the effort.
report.altitudeDesc: Less oxygen, more effort for the same pace: the correction accounts for it.
report.elevationDesc: Climbs and descents brought back to an equivalent pace on the flat.
report.deep: On demand, the in-depth session analysis goes further: cardiac drift, climbing efficiency, share of walking, consistency of your repetitions. Every chart explains how it is built and how to read it.
report.alt: Trail run analysis in the dashboard, with sample data: weather of the run, elevation profile, pace and adjusted pace

weather.title: Weather, before and after
weather.lead: Conditions weigh on every pace. Enduraw records them after each run and gives you the forecast for race day.
weather.afterText: Temperature, wind speed and direction, humidity: the conditions of the run appear in its analysis. Heat and wind go into the adjusted pace.
weather.beforeText: In the pacing plan, the forecast for the hour you will pass each point of the course: temperature, humidity, wind, precipitation, cloud cover, UV index, day and night.
weather.alt: Forecast along an ultra-trail course, aid station by aid station, with sample data: temperature, wind and precipitation
weather.caption: Forecast along the course, sample data

matrix.title: Your runner profile
matrix.lead: The Runner Matrix scores six dimensions out of 100: endurance, uphill, downhill, speed, resilience, physiology. It is built from your Strava history and, with Starter, updates after every run.
matrix.alt: Runner Matrix radar on six dimensions, with sample data
matrix.altPacing: Pacing plan on a phone: target time, moving time, distance and elevation

pacing.title: A plan for race day
pacing.lead: Your pace section by section on the real course, your split times at every aid station, and your nutrition plan: carbs, water and sodium per hour.
pacing.targetDesc: The time you are aiming for, turned into a sustainable pace on each section.
pacing.courseDesc: Gradient and technicality of the terrain: ease off on climbs, push on descents.
pacing.altitudeDesc: The extra effort at the top of the passes.
pacing.delivery: Prepared by the Enduraw team and delivered to your dashboard within 5 working days, with a PDF export for race day. After the finish, compare the plan with your actual race, straight from Strava.
pacing.altLaptop: Pacing plan overview on a laptop, fictitious data: target time, moving time, distance, elevation and pace curve
